channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Kennedy family sues to stop Trump’s triumphal arch, saying it will cast a shadow on John F. Kennedy’s gravesite
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have sued the Trump administration to block the planned 250-foot-tall structure, which they said would “damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials” at Arlington National Cemetery. A Post analysis found that the arch would briefly cover Kennedy’s memorial on 50 days of the year and his eternal flame on 18 days, while touching burial sites across the cemetery on 284 days over the year.

item.title: Hegseth escapes impeachment threat as House Republicans unite to prevent a vote
item.description: The result follows a coordinated effort within the Trump administration, including by the president, to defend the defense secretary. Hegseth held a rare Pentagon news conference Tuesday, during which he appealed directly to the president and his allies in Congress. The attempt to remove him from office had been led by Rep. Thomas Massie, a fellow Republican and frequent critic of President Donald Trump.

item.title: Supreme Court grapples with arguments over the power of federal agencies to impose fines
item.description: The case comes as the high court’s conservative majority has pared back the power of federal regulators in a series of recent cases. But even some conservatives appeared skeptical on Tuesday of going further.

item.title: The Nvidia spy scandal rocked the intelligence world. It’s hardly the first.
item.description: China’s spy service bet on lust and arrogance, and Washington was slow to see the risk.

item.description: The suspect, 41, who had been “entrusted with sensitive information,” was arrested on suspicion of espionage, according to U.S. and British authorities.

item.description: Senate Republicans opted to stick with the South Dakota senator as the leader of the caucus.

item.description: Even basic details remain murky about the background of the Chinese executive, whose affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has rocked the global tech industry.

item.title: Jim Jordan elected to serve as minority leader next year by House Republicans
item.description: The Ohio lawmaker defeated Rep. Steve Scalise (R-Louisiana), in a competitive race for the job. Both tried to become House speaker in 2023.

item.description: Performing in the musical more than 200 times as a child actress, I absorbed themes that I realize now are invaluable.

item.title: At least 19 ICE recruits named in DHS hack were hired despite red flags, including past criminal charges or misconduct allegations
item.description: The Trump administration has onboarded thousands of new officers in an accelerated recruitment effort that has bypassed traditional background checks. The Post performed background checks on about 300 of those new hires after activists in October hacked a DHS employee database and released information about thousands of workers.

item.title: Inflation pace slowed in October, but prices remain high
item.description: The pace of inflation eased on a monthly basis in October, as gas prices saw some relief from their steep climb this year. But food prices rose.

item.title: People are paying thousands for a home upgrade that’s often unnecessary
item.description: Outdated practices and codes are resulting in costly recommendations for larger electrical panels to add appliances such as induction stoves, heat pumps or EV chargers. Yet such panel upgrades are rarely needed, some researchers say.

item.description: The more than 500-mile stretch of road, cameras, vehicle barriers and sensors is planned in and around the park. It is one of the longest and most controversial sections.

item.title: Republicans push to make the most of their time left in control of Congress
